answer.worked: The interior angles at A and B are $180-114=66^\circ$ and $180-134=46^\circ$. The exterior angle at C equals their sum, so $\alpha=66+46=112^\circ$.

answer.worked: Equal sides AB and AC give equal base angles, each $4\alpha$. Hence $\alpha+4\alpha+4\alpha=180^\circ$, so $9\alpha=180^\circ$ and $\alpha=20^\circ$.

answer.worked: The diagonals bisect one another, so EFGH is a parallelogram; the diagonals are also equal, so it is a rectangle. The top half-diagonal triangle is isosceles with base angles $38^\circ$, giving $\beta=180-2(38)=104^\circ$. Adjacent angles give $\alpha=180-104=76^\circ$. At E, the right angle is split into $38^\circ$ and $\gamma$, so $\gamma=90-38=52^\circ$.

answer.worked: The reflex angle and interior angle at H make $360^\circ$, so $\alpha=360-230=130^\circ$. Opposite sides are parallel, so EFGH is a parallelogram. Thus opposite angle $\gamma=130^\circ$, and adjacent angle $\beta=180-130=50^\circ$.
